material_facts: Tippett 80% and Milk 100% add established creative teams and international client access.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold: unresolved financial reliability and current funding. Phantom Digital Effects is a VFX project-services group with recognizable creative capabilities, not yet a demonstrated cash-compounding or recurring-software business. The acquired Tippett and Milk/Lola franchises broaden access to international clients, but the consolidation, purchase accounting and inherited liabilities are not sufficiently reconciled to capitalize headline growth. At the 20 October 2026 cutoff, audited FY26 results are still unavailable.

Three facts dominate. FY25 unbilled revenue of ₹43.63 crore is 42.71% of reported revenue. The main audit opinion is unmodified, but the separate internal-financial-controls opinion is qualified; foreign monetary balances were not restated under AS11 and a ₹14.2766 crore VFX payment awaits matching revenue recognition. FY24/FY25 consolidated operating cash flow is negative despite positive profit. The Sept 2025 acquisition balance sheet then adds ₹126.7704 crore goodwill without a satisfactory public reconciliation.

Counterevidence matters: no borrowing default or reported fraud was identified in the annual audit, management reported subsequent collections, and ₹115.703634 crore CCD funding really arrived in June 2026. This is not a zero-cash or fraud conclusion. It is a failure to bridge that cash to current unrestricted liquidity and the acquired liabilities on reliable accounts. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, excluded from rankings. The persistent poor-cash GQS ceiling of 5 remains operative diagnostically. At the verified ₹95.55 quote, ordinary returns, a buy price and a current enterprise value are unsupported. An optimistic funded illustration is a conditional thought experiment, not a recommendation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Phantom Digital Effects Limited, CIN L92100TN2016PLC103929, ISIN INE0MLZ01019, NSE Emerge symbol PHANTOMFX. Phantom Media Group is a collective brand, not a separately registered replacement issuer. Reporting uses Indian GAAP Accounting Standards in the inspected statements. A potential future Ind AS transition is not treated as completed. Annual FY25 consolidated accounts cover the old perimeter, including Spectre and the small UK operation; Tippett enters from July 2025 and Milk from October 2025.

Cutoff 20 October 2026, with official NSE 19 October closing price ₹95.55, active SM series and 300-share lot. The forecast horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031 using actual days divided by 365.25. Nominal INR pretax investor hurdle 15%, with 12%/18% tests; the model separately illustrates 1% entry and 1% exit friction, not a measured spread. The ₹500,000 reference position is not a judgment about personal suitability. Issued shares are 16,322,800 after 18 October allotment, superseding the stale 15,922,800 security-master count. Mandatory CCD conversion lifts the fully diluted count to 21,731,281.

G1 is Conditional: control and disclosure weaknesses matter, but verified evidence does not establish expropriation or fraud. G2 is Hold: material accounting reliability and stale financials prevent decision-grade valuation. G3 is Hold: cash receipt is verified, survival and unrestricted current funds are not. G4 is Conditional: observed trading exists, but spreads, depth and complete surveillance status are not independently established. Confidence is high in exact identity, filing existence and transcribed numerical facts, lower in economic normalization and current cash. Retrieval after cutoff does not authorize using later events.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Primitive assessments are GOV4, MOAT5, REVNS, DUR5, CAPNS, CASH2, BALNS, EXEC3, EARNNS, RNS, D3, PNS and L6. NS means insufficient evidence, not an average score. Revenue history is visible, but a defensible comparable organic growth measure for the acquired current group is not. Normalized earnings and incremental capital productivity cannot be verified around the goodwill/reserve uplift, cost deferrals and overdue audit. Balance-sheet strength cannot be inferred from June funding alone.

BQS has 68% factor coverage, known contribution 2.74 and missing-factor diagnostic bounds 3.06–5.94. GQS has 30% coverage, known contribution 1.20 and unadjusted bounds 1.90–8.20; persistent CASH2 caps its diagnostic upper bound at 5.00 without creating a point score. IAS has 30% coverage, known contribution 1.20 and bounds 1.90–8.20 because Q, R and P are missing. These are mechanical missing-factor bounds, not confidence intervals. All scores remain NS and all three rankings are ineligible under G2.

The exact framework weights are retained, calculated with Decimal and never redistributed over known factors. One-decimal display uses HALF_UP only after calculation. GOV4 does not activate the governance≤3 cap, and G1 is not a demonstrated Fail. The decisive restriction is financial reliability, independently reinforced by current funding uncertainty. The factor audit below gives two material facts, contrary evidence, sources, confidence and a change condition for every factor. One-point sensitivities show arithmetic exposure without pretending that moving an unsupported score fixes a gate.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Phantom sells visual-effects work for films, series and other content. The practical operating unit is a project or shot package: a client awards work, artists and render resources produce it, reviewers request revisions, and approval milestones permit billing and collection. The disclosed policy recognizes VFX-service revenue on proportionate completion, so recognized revenue can precede an invoice or cash. Work in progress, unbilled revenue, customer acceptance and the recoverability of supplier advances are economically central, not incidental accounting balances.

People, software subscriptions, rendering/compute, delivery supervision and premises drive cost. A pipeline or tool can raise productivity, but savings can also be competed away through lower bid prices. The valuable assets are creative leadership, client access, execution history and reusable workflows. Prestigious film credits do not automatically convey ownership of film IP, a royalty stream or a perpetual studio contract. No separate recurring-platform revenue base or monetized proprietary-content economics is verified, so none receives a platform multiple.

Tippett 80% adds North American relationships and high-end production capability; Milk 100%, including the Lola brand discussed by management, adds European capacity and tax-incentive access. Indian execution may improve blended cost, but transfer pricing and intercompany allocation make standalone margins a poor shortcut to group economics. Consolidation eliminates internal revenue, yet minority ownership, foreign payroll, inherited liabilities and integration costs remain real claims. The model uses explicit equivalent billable-capacity assumptions because no audited, like-for-like artist utilization or revenue-per-artist series is available. Those equivalents are not asserted as actual headcount.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
MOAT5 reflects credible delivery capability and relationships, not a durable monopoly. A trusted VFX team can reduce delivery risk on expensive content; recognized creative supervisors, integrated pipelines and client-security requirements are difficult to reproduce instantly. Acquisitions bring heritage and access that a new Indian vendor would need years to build. These are relevant switching frictions within an active project.

The contrary forces are strong. Clients can allocate the next project to another studio, artists and supervisors are mobile, bidding is competitive and the group has no demonstrated recurring pricing power. Content greenlights, strikes, release delays and customer budgets can leave fixed artist capacity underutilized. AI-assisted production may reduce cost and turnaround time but can also lower entry barriers and pricing. Claimed technology or future content IP receives no separately capitalized optionality until revenue, ownership and incremental cash returns are disclosed.

Basilic is an informative but imperfect peer: FY25 consolidated revenue ₹304.09 crore includes UK acquisition effects; owner PAT ₹37.43 crore is below the ₹45.60 crore group profit because of NCI, while CFO is ₹9.63 crore. Digikore's FY25 total income ₹37.01 crore and loss ₹7.20 crore illustrate a very different utilization outcome in the same broad industry. Neither provides a clean multiple to apply mechanically. The peer check supports using normalized, after-rent project economics and attributable owner earnings, not treating all VFX companies as equivalent high-margin software firms.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reported revenue rises from ₹6.7644 crore in pandemic-affected FY21 to ₹22.3327 crore FY22,₹57.8943 crore FY23,₹89.3305 crore FY24 and ₹102.1579 crore FY25. These rows are deliberately not called a clean six-year organic series: the first years are IPO-restated or standalone, later rows are consolidated, and the most recent current group contains acquisitions absent from FY25. FY25 standalone revenue ₹98.5243 crore grew about 10.29% versus consolidated growth about 14.36%. That is slower than the small-base post-IPO surge.

FY25 revenue includes ₹43.63 crore unbilled, about 42.71% of the total. Reported geographic sales categories show domestic ₹29.7660 crore and international ₹28.7618 crore plus that unbilled category, so assigning all unbilled to international revenue would invent a mix. FY25 billed international revenue is down from ₹58.1585 crore, even as total recognized revenue grows. Completion estimates and invoicing timing are therefore essential to any growth-quality conclusion.

H1 FY26 consolidated revenue ₹84.9789 crore is 139% above the prior comparable reported ₹35.5426 crore, but Tippett contributes and Milk is not yet consolidated. Standalone H1 revenue is about ₹47.11 crore. Management's ₹201.32 crore order book and ₹817 crore bid pipeline are dated October 2025, not current verified orders at the October 2026 cutoff. Bids are not contracted sales; no complete cancellation, payment or margin schedule is supplied. The historical CAGR calculations remain visible below, but REV is NS rather than awarding a maximum score to a changing perimeter and uncertain recognition base.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Scaling requires funding projects before final client acceptance, retaining artists, maintaining software/compute, and absorbing acquired working capital. FY25 receivables ₹85.8823 crore plus WIP₹40.7326 crore already exceed annual sales, before supplier advances ₹35.7896 crore. These are separate assets with different recovery mechanisms; summing them is an exposure view, not a second claim on revenue. Revenue growth without billing discipline can worsen, rather than improve, shareholder economics.

The historical capital diagnostic uses operating EBIT excluding other income, standardized 25.17% NOPAT, and average equity plus borrowing less reported cash. It is a broad accounting proxy, not a verified operating invested-capital return: it includes disputed advances and excludes lease capitalization consistently. FY25 operating EBIT falls while the capital base rises materially. The incremental NOPAT-to-capital change is negative. Acquired goodwill and the unexplained H1 reserves uplift make a forward CAP point score unjustifiable. CAP stays NS, and cash conversion alone already triggers the GQS ceiling.

The scenario model specifies starting revenue ₹180/240/300 crore,0/10/15% growth,8/15/20% operating EBIT margins, and net operating working capital of 100/70/45% of revenue. These are analyst stress assumptions, not management guidance. Maintenance and growth capex, depreciation, NCI, cash tax, debt service and monthly cash floors are explicit. No free growth, automatic debt roll-over, warrant option proceeds or fresh equity rescue is inserted. An additional US$2.7 million subscription into Milk is an intragroup funding transfer; only subsequent external spend affects consolidated cash, and the operating-cash/working-capital assumptions already represent that spend. It is not charged again as acquisition consideration.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Founder-led control creates continuity in a creative business, but financial reporting and capital allocation must catch up with cross-border scale. The FY25 audit committee response acknowledges the customer/vendor onboarding, credit-assessment and procurement-control weakness and describes corrective action. The H1 FY26 reviewer still highlights insufficient overall internal controls; an action plan is not evidence of remediation. FY26 audit approval was repeatedly delayed, and the 6 October 2026 filing still points to 21 October, beyond cutoff.

Director remuneration declined to ₹2.52 crore from ₹3.60 crore, a useful counterpoint to an automatic extraction thesis. Disclosed director loan receipts were ₹7 crore with ₹2.7126 crore ending balance; guesthouse rent to a related party was ₹0.054 crore. These are disclosed transactions, not proof of improper leakage. Repayment priority, terms and subsidiary/intercompany balances should nevertheless be reconciled with the funding plan. The inspected audit reports no borrowing default, wilful defaulter status or reported fraud; bank returns and audit trail provide limited positive checks, not a replacement for contract acceptance evidence.

Execution evidence is mixed. Tippett actually closed July 2025 after earlier announcements, Milk ownership was evidenced October 2025 and Zee funding arrived June 2026. Yet the official November 2025 call could not explain the large goodwill and reserve reconciliation when asked, and current audited accounts remain missing. The report therefore uses GOV4 and EXEC3, not a governance-fraud Fail. Promoter equity at the final warrant allotment is inferable from the filed 7,398,800 shares, around 45.33% issued; it falls further under mandatory CCD dilution. Current encumbrances and effective public float are not fully verified, so no pristine ownership or liquidity claim is made.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The full audit must be read beyond its headline. FY25 standalone and consolidated main opinions are unmodified, but the separate IFC opinion is qualified for acceptance, credit and procurement controls. The auditor also identifies non-restatement of foreign monetary items under AS11, without quantifying the effect, and emphasizes ₹14.2766 crore paid for 3 D/VFX services not yet reflected in P&L pending related revenue recognition. This may be a timing/contract-asset question rather than a permanent loss; it is not safe to assume either outcome. Statutory dues ₹0.0469 crore older than six months are also noted.

FY24/FY25 annual consolidated CFO of−₹54.1751/−₹18.8084 crore compares with PAT ₹24.1123/₹20.2021 crore. H1 FY26 group CFO is−₹18.6183 crore, despite reported PAT ₹20.6855 crore. Historical classifications are not consistent: FY23 CFO includes ₹3.8267 crore short-term borrowing inflow, and the original FY24 standalone CFO includes ₹9.8259 crore borrowing inflow with ₹22.30 crore deposits in investing. Later comparative classifications differ. These differences are not described as missing cash; debt flows and bank-deposit classification are shown separately. Persistent negative operating realization survives those caveats.

Unbilled ₹43.63 crore is already within FY25 receivables ₹85.8823 crore. Billed receivables include ₹28.7066 crore aged 6–12 months and ₹6.1134 crore 1–2 years, without a provision. Management's subsequent collection claims are useful but mix dates and standalone/group scope, so they do not establish current group cash. Interim comparative cash moves from ₹19.0619 crore to ₹18.4319 crore, with ₹0.6300 crore moved into investments. Receivables/OCA reclassification leaves a ₹0.0273 crore total-assets residual. Interim FY25 PAT also differs by ₹0.5434 crore, equal to prior-year tax, while EPS is unchanged. The audited annual figures remain the historical anchor.

At Sept 2025, goodwill ₹126.7704 crore, reserves ₹333.6879 crore and negative NCI₹6.9692 crore need purchase-accounting reconciliation. QIP unutilized certificates total ₹37.4469 crore against group cash ₹35.5209 crore and include an OD-account credit; they cannot be subtracted mechanically to proclaim negative free cash. Current unrestricted cash, inherited liabilities and owner-attributable normalized earnings remain ND. These are material G2/G3 limitations, not assertions of insolvency.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Official ₹95.55 produces issued equity capitalization ₹155.964354 crore and mandatory-diluted capitalization ₹207.642389955 crore. The issued market cap is not a fully diluted valuation, and the fully diluted market cap is not an extra cash liability. Zee's ₹115.703634 crore cash is received at its actual June 2026 date;5,408,481 mandatory shares are included, with only the 0.01% coupon until conversion. Converted principal is not subtracted as debt. The October warrant adds only the final ₹7.41 crore cash because the initial ₹2.47 crore was already in the September 2025 balance sheet.

A current EV, normalized P/E, price/book bargain claim and ordinary IRR are withheld. June funding cannot simply be added to a stale cash balance while ignoring acquisitions, operations and earmarks. Published H1 PAT is not a clean owner earnings run rate, and book equity is distorted by unreconciled purchase accounting. Scenario terminal EV/EBIT multiples 6/10/12 are explicit analyst conventions, not measured peer averages. After-rent EBIT is used consistently; NCI, debt and excess cash are bridged to common equity, with operating reserves retained and no duplicate dividend.

The dated pre-entry bridge tests when money was available. In the base timing illustration, accessible cash begins at ₹17.3947 crore after a purpose reserve; assumed operations, seller payments and inherited-liability settlement breach the ₹10 crore floor before the June CCD. Later cash cannot retroactively cure that breach. The bear also fails. Their no-rescue returns and entry prices are null, even if a terminal-value equation produces a number. The bull assumes unrestricted access to the entire opening balance, positive pre-entry cash generation and late inherited-liability settlement; only that optimistic path passes, producing a large conditional return that is not promoted into R or IAS.

Full annual and monthly rows,12/15/18% hurdle prices, margin-versus-multiple and growth-versus-working-capital surfaces, reverse solves and a discount-rate/terminal-growth DCF are embedded. Mechanical prices behind failed funding gates are diagnostic contingent values, never investable targets. The DCF terminal share and standardized reinvestment are explicit. Proof of reliable accounts and funded cash timing must precede an attractive-price conclusion.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent impairment risk is High. The linked downside is not merely a weak quoted market: delayed approvals defer billing, doubtful receivables and supplier advances consume cash, international artist costs remain fixed, and inherited liabilities demand payment before incoming financing. The same project problems can reduce recognized revenue, earnings, recoverable assets and covenant headroom simultaneously. Unquantified AS11 adjustments, purchase-accounting changes or goodwill impairment could reduce reported equity without an equivalent cash inflow.

The diagnostic bear uses flat ₹180 crore starting revenue,8% EBIT margin,100% operating working capital and 6% capex. It fails the cash floor, so no non-rescue shareholder return is printed. The pre-entry timing stress produces a substantial deficit under early liability settlement; this is an assumed stress, not evidence that the company actually missed payments. The model does not solve the deficit with an unspecified bank facility or new equity. Any recapitalization would require its own price, date, priority and dilution analysis, and could materially impair existing shareholders.

Recovery would depend on collectible contract assets, customer relationships that survive staff turnover, real usable cash and profitable delivery, not the accounting goodwill balance. A severe loss can exceed a modelled price decline because funding failure changes shareholder claims and execution options. Conversely, verified collections and liabilities paid from received CCD money could materially improve the conclusion. Quantified stress therefore belongs beside, not instead of, the evidence gaps. A zero-equity outcome is possible in a severe rescue/restructuring case, but no probability or liquidation recovery point estimate is asserted without an asset-by-asset creditor waterfall.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger outcome is not a present investment thesis. At ₹95.55,5× and 10× imply ₹477.75 and ₹955.50 per share. With 21,731,281 mandatory diluted shares, a 15× exit P/E requires owner earnings around ₹69.21 crore and ₹138.43 crore respectively. At an assumed 12% owner net margin, that means revenue around ₹576.78 crore and ₹1,153.57 crore. Those are arithmetic requirements, not targets, and must be compared with an assumed ₹240 crore current run rate because audited FY26 revenue is unavailable.

Growth in group revenue alone does not establish those outcomes. The acquired perimeter must convert sales into common-owner cash after foreign costs, minority interests, reinvestment, debt service and any future dilution. Mandatory CCD conversion already expands shares by about 33.13% relative to current issued shares and gives new CCD holders about 24.89% of fully diluted equity. The model does not award further rerating merely for becoming a larger international group.

For 5×, a profitable and cash-disciplined scale-up is conceivable in industry terms, but current evidence does not demonstrate the starting earnings or the capital needed.10× requires much more demanding growth and sustained owner margins, without funding dilution eroding the per-share result. Neither outcome receives a probability, score bonus or investment classification. Reassess only after comparable audited perimeter data, documented collections and credible incremental returns exist.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The highest-priority trigger is the next full audited consolidated report with all annexures, not a press release. It must reconcile FY25 and H1 comparative changes, goodwill and reserves, the negative NCI balance, acquired net assets and owner earnings, foreign-currency restatement and the ₹14.2766 crore VFX payment. Obtain project acceptance/billing evidence and collection ageing for unbilled balances and vendor advances. Track whether the auditor confirms controls operating effectively, rather than management merely announcing a policy.

Funding monitoring needs a dated opening-to-current cash bridge: June CCD receipt, October warrant receipt, each acquisition seller tranche, inherited-liability settlement, Milk subscription and actual external use, tax/interest, debt repayment, remaining commitments and unutilized QIP/CCD purposes. Reconcile bank deposits, OD credit, restrictions and debt by entity. No current bank statement is demanded as the only possible proof; audited accounts, independent utilization certificates and sufficiently detailed exchange disclosures could establish the same facts. A clear funds-flow bridge can move G3 without waiting indefinitely for perfect data.

Operating triggers are comparable organic revenue, acceptance-to-billing-to-cash cycle, aged/unbilled receivables, write-offs, project gross margin after revisions, artist utilization and attrition, and maintenance plus growth capex. Confirm which order-book amounts are enforceable awards versus bids and how much is from acquired entities. For capital structure, verify CCD conversion terms and date, updated share listing/trading approvals, further warrants/ESOPs and promoter encumbrances. Recheck lot size, surveillance notices and 20/60-session traded value before implementation. The scheduled 21 October 2026 board date is a future catalyst at this cutoff, not a known outcome.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold, unresolved financial reliability and funding; not investment-ready and excluded from quality, growth-quality and attractiveness rankings. The watchlist case is that the acquired creative franchises and Indian delivery base eventually produce diversified, billable and collected earnings. The current evidence is insufficient to distinguish that outcome from a larger but capital-hungry aggregation of projects and liabilities.

No buy zone, ordinary target price, supported base IRR or position recommendation is supplied. Lower market price alone does not cure a material accounting gate. A verified improvement would require timely audited current accounts, quantified resolution of the audit observations, a defensible acquisition/NCI bridge and a cash timeline that survives realistic collection and liability timing without rescue capital. Once those exist, recompute current cash, debt and dilution rather than carrying forward this diagnostic model unchanged.

Tradability is conditional rather than absent. The 60-session reference supports about 3.80 days at 5% participation for ₹5 lakh; the more recent 20-session figure is 6.03 days. Whole-lot positions nearest that amount are ₹487,305 for 5,100 shares and ₹515,970 for 5,400 shares. These historical capacity estimates do not guarantee an exit in a one-sided or restricted market. L starts at 7 under the 60-day rule and is reduced to 6 for lot granularity, worsening recent capacity and unverified spread/depth. G4 remains an independent implementation condition.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources are the complete FY23/FY24/FY25 annual reports, IPO restated statements, H1 FY26 financials and reviewer reports, official earnings-call transcripts, acquisition/financing exchange disclosures, and dated NSE security and bhavcopy files. Source URLs, hashes, exact locators and original paraphrased evidence are retained. Third-party search results were used only for discovery; rolling prices and postcutoff results were not used. Historical values are financial facts, not reproduced annual-report prose. Raw PDFs, extracted document text, screenshots, identities of ordinary shareholders and credentials are excluded from both archives.

Every major assumption is separated from an observed fact. The current operating run rate, cost structure, future margins, utilization equivalents, working-capital intensity, payment schedules, FX 90/USD, NCI economic allocation and cash reserves are analyst illustrations. No audited capital schedule proves those inputs. The historical table preserves source scopes and conflicting classifications instead of harmonizing them silently. The absence of verified current borrowing ratings, complete encumbrance data or surveillance status is a disclosed gap, not a claim that no restriction or risk exists.

The canonical dossier embeds all historical rows, calculated metrics, model inputs, annual/monthly funding rows and sensitivity outputs. The source-safe seed plus deterministic builders reconstruct every generated research output after deletion, in both compact and full archives. Arithmetic recovery verifies the research artifact, not the authenticity of the source documents or the truth of management claims. Open questions are enumerated by gate and monitoring trigger; the most important unresolved items are current audited accounts, purchase accounting, contract-asset collectibility and dated unrestricted funding. Any later publication or ranking must retain these limitations and the 20 October cutoff.

summary:
Hold: unresolved financial reliability and current funding. Phantom Digital Effects is a VFX project-services group with recognizable creative capabilities, not yet a demonstrated cash-compounding or recurring-software business. The acquired Tippett and Milk/Lola franchises broaden access to international clients, but the consolidation, purchase accounting and inherited liabilities are not sufficiently reconciled to capitalize headline growth. At the 20 October 2026 cutoff, audited FY26 results are still unavailable.

Three facts dominate. FY25 unbilled revenue of ₹43.63 crore is 42.71% of reported revenue. The main audit opinion is unmodified, but the separate internal-financial-controls opinion is qualified; foreign monetary balances were not restated under AS11 and a ₹14.2766 crore VFX payment awaits matching revenue recognition. FY24/FY25 consolidated operating cash flow is negative despite positive profit. The Sept 2025 acquisition balance sheet then adds ₹126.7704 crore goodwill without a satisfactory public reconciliation.

Counterevidence matters: no borrowing default or reported fraud was identified in the annual audit, management reported subsequent collections, and ₹115.703634 crore CCD funding really arrived in June 2026. This is not a zero-cash or fraud conclusion. It is a failure to bridge that cash to current unrestricted liquidity and the acquired liabilities on reliable accounts. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, excluded from rankings. The persistent poor-cash GQS ceiling of 5 remains operative diagnostically. At the verified ₹95.55 quote, ordinary returns, a buy price and a current enterprise value are unsupported. An optimistic funded illustration is a conditional thought experiment, not a recommendation.
